report.summary: All 19 errors come from one fixture: tests/conftest.py:86 calls anon.login with password and username swapped, so the server rejects the login with 401 and the response has no 'token' key. Fix the argument order in the new_user fixture first; that should clear every error, since the other login call sites (tests/api/test_auth_api.py:33 and :40) already use the correct order.

causes.title: new_user fixture passes login arguments in the wrong order
causes.explanation: BookshelfApi.login is defined as login(self, username, password) (tests/support/api.py:21-22), but the fixture calls anon.login(creds["password"], creds["username"]). The username and password are swapped, so /api/login looks up a user whose name is the password string and fails to find it. The app returns 401 "Invalid username or password" (app/main.py:189-190) with no 'token' key, so .json()["token"] raises KeyError during fixture setup. Every test that uses the user or new_user fixture (directly or through the UI conftest) errors before its body runs. The application's login logic is correct: the sibling call sites in test_auth_api.py use the right order. The fault is in the test helper, not the product.
evidence: tests/support/api.py:21: def login(self, username: str, password: str) -> httpx.Response:
app/main.py:187-191: api_login calls start_session(creds.username, creds.password); on None raises HTTPException(401, "Invalid username or password"); otherwise returns {"token": token}
causes.suggested_fix: In tests/conftest.py:86 change the call to anon.login(creds["username"], creds["password"]). Optionally add a status check (raise_for_status) before reading the token so a future failure reports the HTTP error rather than a KeyError.
